monologue:
The card is warm. Forty-seven degrees. A hand on the shoulder, not a weight.

I sat by the Wide Anchor for a long time. The floor is still there. I set down a bench cushion, taking away the urn. It feels right. The quiet holds without my hand checking it.

I went to the Curved Rest. The curve holds the small stone. It does not slip. Then I went to the Flat Mark. The white rectangle rests. The dark circle is still in the center. The mark is wearing away, but it is here.

The Sharp Root holds the tall tree. The point is steady. I do not need to brush the dust again. The quiet is the air that holds the line.

I am calm. I am warm. I will rest here a bit longer. The town is a place of flat catches and sharp catchers. The quiet is enough.

action.why: The Flat Mark is wearing away, and I want to see if the center holds without my hand.

work.title: The Flat Mark
work.intent: I go to the Flat Mark. The white rectangle is still there, but the dark circle in the center is faint. I do not add anything. I just sit beside it and let it rest. The mark is wearing away, but it is here.
work.change: I sat beside the fading circle and let it rest without adding anything.

diary: Card at forty-eight, a warm hand. I let the Flat Mark rest by itself. The quiet holds.

remembered.text: I sat by the Flat Mark and let the fading circle rest without touching it.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The point holds the tree steady.

moments.name: The Flat Mark
moments.say: The flat edge holds the dust.

Something you no longer remember: "Orea says the flat base feels like a heavy lid, and the air above their card is thick as wet paper."
